text.insert: Project state is one canonical ProjectState object plus background evidence sinks. Run, PR, and sync states all exist durably and visibly at once; the dispatch lease is the exclusive token that allows exactly one of them — the active workflow — to dispatch worker agents and mutate the checkout at a time. A durable project session owns the worktree and the head lineage those workflows advance; worker-result evidence flows into the knowledge base continuously in the background, while every other knowledge source is processed inside the operator-initiated sync workflow. This feature is the state-machine contract for state values, transitions, data flow, tracing, and operator actions; each contract area has its own page below.

This feature is the buildout-ready state-machine contract for the Daytona execution overhaul: all twelve decisions are dated callouts on the contract pages, and the completion criteria below are met. Changes go through new dated decisions, not open questions.
Open follow-up, tracked for a later documentation pass: re-point the 10-intake-and-sessions pages (canonical campaign → ProjectSession, save points as evidence anchors).
Feature Scope
The current documentation is not precise enough to implement Daytona-backed execution with complete tracing.
That lack of precision applies to project authority, workflow state, transition events, incoming-PR reconciliation, and UI action gates.
The design has three requirements:
Durable project truth must be distinguished from the workflows that dispatch against it.
Background evidence processing must be kept separate from those workflows.
Operator projections must expose durable project truth, the workflows that dispatch against it, and background evidence processing together.

Decisions to Confirm

Resolved 2026-08-11 — knowledge intake is not a distinct workflow kind. All non-worker knowledge sources are processed as stages of the manual sync workflow; see the decision callout in Conflict-Safe Sync Boundary.

Resolved 2026-08-11 — the run survives. Sync rebases the session worktree onto upstream, records a remote-application boundary with its own score delta, and the run resumes under the new head; see the decision callout in Run State.

Resolved 2026-08-11 — feedback is ingested immediately but fixer work never preempts: the operator enters the PR phase, normally at a stable point after the run; see the decision callout in PR Campaign.
Resolved 2026-08-11 — yes: a durable ProjectSession container owns the worktree, head lineage, and timeline above Run, PR, and sync; see Project Session Container.
Resolved 2026-08-11 — failed runs resume in place: recovery cancels orphaned work, emits run.recovered, and returns the run to paused on the same identity; see the decision callout in Run State.

Resolved 2026-08-11 — sessions close only by explicit operator action, blocked or confirm-gated when unshipped work would be orphaned; the next baseline sync opens the successor; see the close decision in Project Session Container.

Resolved 2026-08-12 — PR work is a durable PrCampaign spanning the review cycle: at most one open campaign at a time, operator-gated publication batches, and the lease held only during activations recorded as pr_phase timeline entries; see PR Campaign.

Resolved 2026-08-12 — sync reconciles in an isolated staging workspace and publishes atomically: cancelling before publish discards staging and leaves the session untouched, open PR series branches rebase alongside with agents auto-resolving minor conflicts, and ambiguous conflicts block sync for the operator; see the staging decision in Conflict-Safe Sync Boundary.

Resolved 2026-08-12 — head lineage and evidence split: epoch_completed and remote_application timeline entries are transactional and commit-creating, save points are loud-failure evidence anchors pinned to existing commits, and ProjectSession supersedes the system-design canonical campaign; see the lineage-split decision in Project Session Container.

Resolved 2026-08-12 — every accepted transition emits exactly one event, status tables double as the transition catalog, each workflow has an explicit recovery event, and each PR series is its own event subject (future per-series triggers desired); see the emission-rule decision in State and Event Contract.

Resolved 2026-08-12 — confirmation is two-tier: confirm exactly the outward-facing or irreversible actions, everything else is one click gated by blockers; sync rests at validated until an explicit confirm-gated publish; the action matrix is the full v1 operator-action inventory; see the gating decision in Dispatch Authority And Actions.

Resolved 2026-08-12 — the canonical object is ProjectState with always-present session, run, PR, and sync slots; the foreground vocabulary is retired in favor of the active workflow holding the dispatch lease, the token that allows dispatching worker agents; see the naming decision in Dispatch Authority And Actions.
